PhyLayer holds a list of PhyDevice shared_ptrs
registered on it. Two default phys are created in
A device/controller can be on several phys at once.

RSSI between two devices is fabricated by
Once the two controllers have a direct ACL link
For BLE, an established ACL connection between the two
controllers is emulated at the PhyLayer level by the
LLCP packets (the Rust link layer's LLCP state machine,
e.g. LL_VERSION_IND / LL_FEATURE_REQ etc.), and the ACL
data frames sent by the hosts ride along as "ACL" type
HandleAcl -> sends ACL data to HOST B
On the BR/EDR PhyLayer, controllers exchange LMP packets
(PAGE, PAGE_RESPONSE, LMP procedures) — these are shaped
by the Rust LinkManager (rust/src/lmp) and reach the air
via the same PhyDevice -> PhyLayer -> broadcast route.
A packet is always broadcast, never unicast
There is no direct socket between controller A and
controller B. Sending a link-layer packet from one
controller simply calls into the shared PhyLayer which
iterates its device list and delivers a copy to every
